discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 041329
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
929 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Primarily dry conditions are expected for the next several 
  days.

- Today, notable temperature difference northwest to southeast 
  as a cold front moves through. Highs will range from the 
  mid-60s to mid-70s, respectively.

- Cold Tuesday morning with lows dipping down to the 30s for
  some locations.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 231 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

Weak disturbance moving eastward across Lake Michigan this 
morning with clouds and a few rain showers associated with it.
Did add some light rain showers this morning over northern half
of Berrien County in Michigan where a few showers may make it 
to the surface as it pushes through. Radar imagery does show
some returns especially over the lake but with the drier low
levels much of it is likely virga. Also, adjusted low
temperatures up this morning by a few degrees as WAA ahead of
this disturbance along with some moisture indicated by slightly
higher surface dew points. This and the addition of some clouds
moving through with the disturbance will keep temperatures a tad
warmer than originally expected this morning. Temperatures 
currently as of 2:30 AM EDT are still in the low 50s here at the
office. 

A cold front behind this disturbance will move through the area
later today and this will keep high temperatures a bit cooler
(in the upper 60s) for northwestern areas while highs will warm
into the low 70s further south and east. Clearing skies will
also take place later today with the cooler and drier airmass
moving into the area behind the cool front. 

Dry weather will then be expected through the remainder of the
work week into next weekend and a cooler start to the week with
lows back into the 40s on Monday morning with highs then only
getting into the low to mid 60s. Then a reinforcing shot of
drier and cooler air arrives Monday night with temperatures
dropping into the low 40s and even getting in some locations to
the upper 30s. Will still have to watch this carefully as
clear skies and light winds will allow for good radiational 
cooling and if a bit drier air moves in would allow for a bit
colder temperatures perhaps into the mid 30s for some locations.
Still would recommend if you have temperature sensitive plants
or animals that you protect them Monday night into Tuesday 
morning out of an abundance of caution. 

A northwesterly flow aloft envelopes the region by midweek
becoming more zonal late in the week with a high amplitude ridge
building eastward into the central CONUS by next weekend. This
will provide for a warming trend from Tuesday into next weekend
with highs by Saturday and Sunday getting into the mid to upper
70s. Perhaps a few locations along the southern tier of our CWA
could see close to 80. The next chance of precipitation looks to
be late in the weekend with a southern stream disturbance from
Texas moving northeastward into the region.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 603 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

A weak cold front will move through the area today but very dry
low levels will keep precipitation at bay. Passing midlevel 
clouds and a wind shift will be the main impacts but conditions 
will remain VFR with northwesterly wind gusts generally less 
than 20 kts.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 041243

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0743 AM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 041300Z - 051200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE
   FLORIDA PANHANDLE...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few rotating thunderstorms are possible today across the coastal
   Florida Panhandle.

   ...Florida Panhandle...
   A stalled/slow-southeastward-moving surface front will reside across
   the Southeast and Deep South today, with a very moist airmass
   persisting along and to its south, featuring Precipitable Water
   values in excess of 2 inches. Scattered showers/thunderstorms are
   common early today south of the front, including across the northern
   half of the Gulf. There are some guidance indications, most notably
   recent NAM runs, that weak offshore surface low development may
   occur today, with a related developing enhancement to the low-level
   flow/SRH. Should this trend materialize, showers/thunderstorms will
   have the potential to exhibit brief, transient low-level
   circulations, mainly near the coast, with a related waterspout/brief
   tornado potential.

   ..Guyer/Dean.. 10/04/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 040521

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1221 AM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely across the USA on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will continue to deepen as it moves eastward across
   Quebec on Monday, with the speed max at the base of the trough
   sweeping across the Northeast. Behind this trough, northwest flow
   will persist from the Northern Plains into the Great Lakes, with a
   weak midlevel trough moving across the Great Basin.

   At the surface, a large area of high pressure will provide stable
   conditions to much of the central and eastern States, with the more
   substantial low-level moisture and instability relegated to the Gulf
   Coast area. Scattered thunderstorms will thus be possible along the
   northern Gulf Coast, and across much of Florida, though severe
   storms are unlikely.

   Elsewhere, sporadic lightning flashes may occur over parts of
   southern CO, and into parts of NV where cool air aloft will steepen
   lapse rates. Instability will be weak, as will low-level wind
   fields. A few strong gusts cannot be ruled out due to the deeply
   mixed boundary layer.

   ..Jewell.. 10/04/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 040649

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0149 AM CDT Sun Oct 04 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep upper trough will quickly move out of eastern Quebec and New
   England on Tuesday, with a secondary lower-amplitude trough diving
   southeast across Ontario and Upper Great Lakes. This northwest flow
   regime will generally maintain high pressure over much of the
   central and eastern CONUS, with northeast surface winds near the
   Gulf and Atlantic Coasts. As such, available moisture and
   instability will remain largely offshore, except over FL where
   afternoon thunderstorms are possible. Severe storms are unlikely due
   to the weak shear/lapse rate environment.

   Elsewhere, scattered showers and thunderstorms may affect the
   eastern Great Basin into western CO, as a weak midlevel wave moves
   over the area with cool temperatures aloft. Severe storms are
   unlikely given weak instability and shear.

   ..Jewell.. 10/04/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
